import java.util.*;
import java.math.BigInteger;

public class Main {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        Scanner sc = new Scanner(System.in);
        if (!sc.hasNextInt()) return;
        int p = sc.nextInt();
        int k = sc.nextInt();
        
        System.out.println(solve(p, k));
    }

    public static long solve(int p, int k) {
        long num = 0;
        Set<Integer> used = new HashSet<>();
        for (int j = 0; j < p; j++) {
            if (!used.contains(j)) {
                num++;
                int i = j;
                while (!used.contains(i)) {
                    used.add(i);
                    i = (int) (((long) i * k) % p);
                }
            }
        }
        
        long exponent = num - (k != 1 ? 1 : 0);
        return power(p, exponent, 1000000007);
    }

    public static long power(long base, long exp, long mod) {
        if (exp < 0) return 0; // Based on Python's pow behavior for negative exp in this context
        long res = 1;
        base %= mod;
        while (exp > 0) {
            if (exp % 2 == 1) res = (res * base) % mod;
            base = (base * base) % mod;
            exp /= 2;
        }
        return res;
    }
}
